prompt:
I need the front end for Givehours. A personal planner for people who volunteer with several nonprofits at once, gathering the shifts each organization posts alongside the volunteer's own commitments so they can choose what to take on each month.

Who's using it: Theo Lindqvist, 34, an insurance claims adjuster who volunteers in his spare time with three organizations: a regional food bank's warehouse, an adult literacy program where he has promised to tutor 8 hours a month, and a cat shelter. Nobody makes him use this; he set it up himself after double-booking twice last spring.

What they're doing right now: December shift sign-ups opened today at noon for both the food bank and the cat shelter, and the popular holiday-week warehouse slots usually fill within two days. Theo wants to claim shifts for December while keeping the weekends of Dec 12–13 and Dec 25–27 free for family, fitting his two weekly tutoring sessions with his learner Mrs. Okonjo around her new evening work schedule, and not taking on more than about 20 hours total. He also needs to swap out of a Dec 3 shelter shift that clashes with a work trip.

What's in the system at this point: December 2026. Food bank (Cascade Harvest Food Bank): 46 open warehouse and distribution shifts, 3–4 hours each, with location (Main Warehouse or Eastside Pantry), role (sorting, packing, driver's assistant) and spots left (e.g., 'Dec 19 9 am–12 pm sorting – 4 of 20 left'). Cat shelter (Whisker Haven): 31 shifts, 2 hours each, by role (feeding, socializing, adoption-event helper), with Theo already booked Dec 3 and Dec 17, 6–8 pm. Literacy program (ReadUp Adult Learning): commitment of 8 h/month with learner Grace Okonjo; her new availability is Tue and Thu after 7 pm or Sat mornings. Theo's personal commitments: work trip Dec 2–4 to Spokane, family weekends Dec 12–13 and Dec 25–27, standing Wednesday climbing night. Running totals: November hours 22.5 (food bank 9, shelter 6, tutoring 7.5); year to date 214 hours.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
